title: Tenant-aware span reshaper and schema probing for cross-backend compatibility
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a lightweight span reshaper service that normalizes incoming spans from OTLP, Jaeger, and Zipkin clients into a canonical internal schema, while probing for incoming schema variants and exposing per-tenant mapping rules. Goal: reduce downstream sink incompatibilities (Tempo, Jaeger, external observability vendors) and avoid customer regressions when we change storage schemas or enable new enrichment. The reshaper must be low-latency (<2ms median extra), support per-tenant mapping overrides, and be able to run in the ingest tier as a sidecar or centrally as a small fleet.
background: We continue to see customer complaints and internal test failures when spans emitted by legacy SDKs include vendor-specific tags (e.g., 'jaeger.tags', 'zipkin.shared') or when downstream sinks expect specific fields. Current workarounds are brittle: downstream sink adapters do expensive translations or we rely on ingestion-time heuristics inside Tempo connectors. This ticket formalizes a reusable reshaping layer plus a schema probe to detect incoming variants and select the right mapping rules. This will make future sink onboarding (third-party vendors) and schema migrations less error-prone.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical schema defined (doc link) and mapping spec for common vendor variants
Per-tenant mapping rules stored in config service and applied at ingest
Schema probe can classify >95% of incoming traces into known variants within first 5 spans
Added latency from reshaper <=2ms median and P99 <10ms on 95th percentile load test
End-to-end tests validating reshaped spans show correct fields for Tempo and Jaeger sinks
Security review completed and KMS keys handled for any tenant-specific overrides
design_notes: Will use a small rule engine (compiled patterns) rather than a full JS sandbox to keep latency low
Probe stage samples first N spans per connection to infer schema, caches result per-tenant for 10m
Mapping rules allow renames, type coercion, prefix stripping, and controlled field drops
Fallback: if probe yields unknown variant, tag span with 'reshaper.unknown_variant' and forward raw
We avoid any per-tokenizable payload alterations (no body mutation) to keep compatibility with existing query tooling
implementation_plan: Week 1: Spec canonical schema and common vendor mapping patterns; design data model for tenant configs
Week 2: Implement probe + rule engine core and unit tests; local perf harness
Week 3: Integrate with ingest path; add per-tenant config lookup and caching; staging deploy
Week 4: Compatibility tests against Tempo and Jaeger connectors; load testing and spike review
Week 5: Security review, docs, runbook, rollout via canary and platform flag
progress_updates: 2025-01-17: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and connectors teams. Agreed on canonical schema draft (Confluence: /confluence/display/OBS/Canonical-Span-Schema).
2025-01-22: Prototype of rule engine completed (Go). Local microbenchmark shows ~0.9ms median add latency for simple rename rules.
2025-01-28: Probe logic implemented; initial heuristics for Jaeger vs Zipkin vs generic OTLP pass basic fuzz tests. Cache TTL defaulted to 10 minutes to balance churn.
2025-02-02: Integrated with ingest path behind feature flag 'reshaper-v1'. Staging traces show correct renames for two customers (tenant: acme-corp, tenant: beta-labs).
2025-02-05: Perf test run at 10k rps with realistic span size: median extra latency 1.8ms, P99 at 9.6ms. Noted increased GC noise under heavy batching; follow-up to tune memory pools.
open_issues: Memory allocation pattern in rule engine causes GC spikes at 20k+ rps; Mateo to prototype object pooling
Operator UX for per-tenant rules needs a safe validation UI in Console before broad rollout
Need to add e2e golden trace tests for vendor-specific baggage fields (e.g., jaeger.operation)
reviews_and_feedback: Design review 2025-01-20: PM (Riley Carter) requested explicit opt-out for tenants who want raw pass-through
Security review request submitted 2025-01-30 (ticket SEC-2321). Security asked for threat model and KMS usage plan.
Infra review 2025-02-03: suggested moving probe cache into edge nodes to avoid cross-region lookups for latency-sensitive tenants
runbook_notes: Feature flag 'reshaper-v1' controls activation per-cluster; immediate rollback should toggle flag off and flush probe cache
If unknown_variant rates exceed 5% for a tenant, auto-disable reshaping and alert on channel #observability-ops
Provide a utility to export sample spans for tenant debugging: go run tools/export_samples --tenant=<id>
postmortem_and_learning: From a small incident during staging (2025-01-31) we learned we must tag spans with original schema metadata to enable debugging without losing raw values
Decision: always include 'reshaper.orig_schema' and 'reshaper.mapping_version' tags when a mapping is applied
notes: Make mapping rules idempotent and reversible where possible to support rollbacks
Plan to provide an API so tenants can preview how their spans will be reshaped before enabling
Consider future extension: enrichment hooks for adding tenant metadata from lookup service
